backlog.spec: In solve(), change the kick disc radius draw from rng.uniform(0.15, 0.35) to rng.uniform(0.10, 0.25), exposed as two module constants KICK_R_MIN and KICK_R_MAX. If the disc contains fewer than 2 circles (m.sum() < 2), redraw p and R (loop until at least 2 are selected) so that no SLSQP call is wasted on a null kick. Nothing else changes. The aim is that smaller kicks keep more of the incumbent structure, so each re-optimisation is cheaper and more often lands in a neighbouring better basin.
backlog.title: Smaller kick disc radius range

backlog.spec: Instead of one incumbent, keep up to 3 elite packings in solve(). Seed them with 3 independent random starts. Then each iteration pick one elite uniformly with rng, apply the existing disc kick and _solve_once, clip and repair, and if the result beats the elite it came from, replace that elite. Every 20 iterations, overwrite the worst elite with a copy of the best. Return the best elite at the end. This keeps diversity early while concentrating effort on the best basin later.
backlog.title: Small elite population of packings

backlog.spec: Replace the disc-radius selection in the kick with a count-based selection: draw p uniform in the unit square and k = rng.integers(2, 7) (2 to 6 inclusive), and select the k circles whose centres are nearest to p. Set R to the distance from p to the k-th nearest centre plus that circle's radius, then re-randomise the selected centres uniformly in the disc of radius R around p (clipped to [0, 1]) and set their radii to 0, exactly as now. Then run the same phase-2 SLSQP and the same greedy acceptance. This fixes the kick size in circles rather than in area, so that corner and edge kicks are not systematically smaller than interior kicks.
backlog.title: Kick the k nearest circles instead of a fixed disc

backlog.spec: With probability 0.5, choose the kick centre p as the emptiest point of the current best packing instead of a uniform random point: sample 500 points uniformly in the unit square, compute for each the clearance = min(min over circles of (distance to centre - radius), distance to the nearest wall), and take the point with the largest clearance as p. Otherwise draw p uniformly as now. The rest of the kick (disc radius R uniform in [0.15, 0.35], re-randomising the centres inside the disc, radii set to 0, phase-2 SLSQP, repair, greedy acceptance) is unchanged. Wasted space marks where the local arrangement is suboptimal.
backlog.title: Aim kicks at the largest hole

backlog.spec: Make each kick cheaper by optimising only the affected region first. After re-randomising the circles in the disc (mask m), define the free set F as the circles in m plus all circles whose centre is within R + 0.15 of p. Run SLSQP on only the centres and radii of F, maximising their radius sum, with the other circles held fixed: constraints are pair gaps within F, gaps between F and fixed circles, wall constraints for F and r >= 0 for F (maxiter 100). Write the result back into the full vector, then run the existing full phase-2 SLSQP only if the sub-solve's total sum is within 0.01 of the best sum; otherwise discard the kick. Repair and greedy acceptance are unchanged. The sub-solve has about a third of the variables, so many more kicks fit in the time.
backlog.title: Restricted local sub-solve after a kick

backlog.spec: Both minimize calls in _solve_once currently use finite-difference gradients, which costs about 79 constraint evaluations per iteration. Supply exact derivatives. For the objective pass jac returning a constant vector (zeros for centres, -1 for radii; in phase 1 zeros with -1 at index 2n). For the constraints add a 'jac' entry to the constraint dict returning a dense matrix with rows in the same order as cons/cons_eq: for pair (i,j) with unit vector u=(ci-cj)/max(d,1e-12), the row has +u in ci's columns, -u in cj's columns, and -1 in the r_i and r_j columns (or -2 in the t column in phase 1); wall rows are +/-1 on the coordinate and -1 on the radius (or t); the r>=0 rows are identity. Preallocate the constant parts once per call and only refill the pair block. Change nothing else, so that the saved time turns into many more kicks in the same budget.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Add a second kick type, chosen with probability 0.5 instead of the disc kick. Pick 1 to 3 circles (rng), favouring small ones: sample without replacement with probability proportional to 1/(r+0.02). For each, remove it and reinsert it at the point of largest free space: sample 2000 uniform points in the square with rng, compute for each point min(distance to walls, min over the remaining circles of distance to centre minus radius), and place the centre at the argmax with radius 0. Then call _solve_once with this start, as the disc kick does. Keep the existing disc kick for the other half of iterations.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert-in-largest-hole kick

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed kick radius range by an adaptive mix of kick sizes. Keep a list of three kick types: (1) the current disc kick with R in [0.12, 0.2], (2) the current disc kick with R in [0.2, 0.35], (3) swap: pick two circles whose radii differ by more than 0.01, exchange their centres, set both radii to 0.9 * min of the two, and add Gaussian jitter of sd 0.01 to all centres. Keep counts of tries and of improvements of best per type, and choose the type for each iteration with probability proportional to (improvements + 1) / (tries + 3), sampled with rng. All kicks end with _solve_once from the kicked start as now.
backlog.title: Small-set swap and jitter kicks with adaptive size

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random initial centres in _solve_once (when start is None) by a jittered structured layout: with rng choose one of (a) a hexagonal layout with rows of alternating 5 and 6 or 6 and 5 circles trimmed or padded to n points, scaled to fit [0.1, 0.9]^2, or (b) a 5x5 grid plus extra points at random cell corners to reach n. Add Gaussian jitter of sd 0.02 to every centre, clip to [INIT_LOW, 1 - INIT_LOW], then run phase 1 and phase 2 as now. The function must work for any n by generating at least n lattice points and keeping a random subset of n.
backlog.title: Structured initial layouts

backlog.spec: Change the acceptance rule of the kick loop to late-acceptance hill climbing. Keep a separate `cur` (the walk state that kicks start from) and `best` (the best valid packing ever, which is returned). Keep a list `hist` of length L = 10 initialised with the first solution's sum. At kick number i, with candidate sum s: accept the candidate as cur if s >= hist[i % L] or s >= cur_sum; then set hist[i % L] = cur_sum. Always update best if s > best_sum. Kicks are generated from cur, not best. The disc kick, the SLSQP solve and _repair stay unchanged.
backlog.title: Late-acceptance hill climbing for the kick walk

memo: Helped: changes to how each solve searches. Slot 8 (equal-radius SLSQP before the free solve) gave -2.6311/-2.6311. Slot 35 (local disc re-randomisation kick) is the incumbent at -2.6343/-2.6354 (delta -0.0037, 2 runs, mean -2.6349). Local-search walks beat fresh restarts: slot 11 gave -2.6354/-2.6334 and slot 27 gave -2.6341/-2.6324. Replica exchange (-2.6348) and the two-island model (-2.6349) tie the incumbent, so more chain machinery adds nothing. No effect (+0.0000): TIME_FRACTION 0.93, LP repair, warm restarts, successive halving. Hurt: radius-weighted restarts (+0.0165), log-barrier (+0.0045), L-BFGS-B penalty (+0.0034), MAX_ITER 1000 (+0.0019). Start-diversity tweaks are exhausted. Next: tune the kick size, disc radius and acceptance rule of slot 35, and polish the best packing at the end. Replicate any gain, since noise sd is 0.0023. Keep the code simple.
